tasks.title: Recover generation switches and configuration effects
tasks.goal: Preserve truthful old/new/partial states across interrupted activation, rollback and repair.
steps: Partition staged payloads, activation pointer, mutable config and external effects into named journal domains with retained before-images where available.
Inject failures before/after pointer switch and each configuration write; implement observe/recover/rollback without re-executing unknown effects.
Keep previous usable manager/recovery artifacts pinned and report third-state drift rather than overwriting it.
positive_cases: Interrupted pointer activation recovers to an evidenced usable generation.
Rollback restores generation/config only within proven reversible effects.
negative_cases: Unknown external effect is called rolled back because files were deleted.
User edits after failure are overwritten by stale before-images.
checks: TO CREATE: crash-prefix, third-state and retained-manager recovery fixtures.
acceptance: Every injected failure exposes completed/pending/uncertain effects and an exact safe next action.
Rollback does not imply mutable database contents were reverted.
tasks.safe_stop: A usable prior generation and complete journal remain available for each failure prefix.
notes: Planned permanent destination: vibevm/vibespecs/common/PROP-064-runtime-package-management.xml; forward metadata only.
The environment/ module is a proposed composition cell in the existing orchestrator; its owning export file is included for registration. Refine the perimeter before touching any additional crate.

Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

tasks.title: Collect only unreferenced owned runtime content
tasks.goal: Implement explicit GC plans that respect shared, pinned, live and recovery references.
steps: Compute GC candidates from generation/dependency/operation/live-process/recovery roots using exact object IDs and current leases.
Prepare and apply contained deletion with root/generation revalidation; maintain alias-root fencing against concurrent activation.
Test stale plans, retained old versions, shared objects, mutable data and failed cleanup; expose byte/reference reasons through ETO.
positive_cases: Only an unreferenced owned generation and exclusive payloads are removed.
A running command or recovery-required operation protects its closure.
negative_cases: A concurrent activation makes a previously unused object live before deletion.
Global cache/prune cleanup deletes unrelated user or Docker resources.
checks: TO CREATE: live-reference, concurrent-GC and ownership-bound deletion tests.
acceptance: GC never deletes mutable user data or shared/live/pinned/recovery content.
Plan and result identify exactly what was and was not deleted.
tasks.safe_stop: Deletion journal and remaining roots are consistent; failed cleanup is retryable within exact ownership.
